subject: Intermittent egress constraint — regional traffic reshuffle & guidance
messages:
From: Sally Torres <sally.torres@pulseai.com>
To: support@redwood.example, irene.choi@redwood.example
Cc: infra@pulseai.com
Date: 2026-08-30T03:12:00Z
Subject: High 5xx rate and latency spikes affecting EU endpoints

Hi team,

We're seeing a spike in 5xx responses and elevated tail latency for requests routed to eu-west-1 over the last 30 minutes. Error rate peaked around 18% (our synthetic checks and live traffic). We started seeing this at ~02:40 UTC. Can you confirm if anything on your side is impacted, or if there's a routing issue upstream?

Quick details:
- Tenant: pulseai-prod
- Endpoint: model.redwood.example/v1/generate (region preference: eu)
- Sample request IDs: req_0981f, req_09a4c
- We can failover to us-east-1 if you recommend it, but would like guidance on whether KV cache or session affinity will be preserved.

Thanks,
Sally
Sally Torres
Head of Platform Reliability, Pulse AI

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>
To: irene.choi@redwood.example, jordan.blake@redwood.example, naomi.feldman@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-30T03:18:00Z
Subject: Fwd: High 5xx rate and latency spikes affecting EU endpoints

Irene / Jordan / Naomi — forwarding Pulse AI's report. Initial checks: Cloud provider telemetry shows egress queueing on several peering interfaces into eu-west-1 (packet drop + retransmits). This looks like an upstream peering saturation event, not our model runtime.

Immediate recommendation:
- Push a customer-facing advisory with a clear option to change region preference to us-east-1 (best recovery path) and apac as a secondary fallback.
- Provide a short snippet for their app to set a region header and update DNS TTL if they want a manual switch.
- Coordinate KV cache expectations: changing region will preserve tenant caches for cached prompts if they shift to a compatible runtime; we should call that out.

I've attached the quick runbook (traffic-shift-runbook.pdf) and a short checklist. Can someone draft the external note to Pulse? Jordan, can you confirm the estimated RTO if the provider resolves egress within 2 hours? Naomi, can you collect tail RTTs and 5xx timeslices for their tenant so we can include numbers?

-Ben

Attachment: traffic-shift-runbook.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.example>
To: Sally Torres <sally.torres@pulseai.com>
Cc: infra@pulseai.com, ben.carter@redwood.example, jordan.blake@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-30T03:28:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx rate and latency spikes affecting EU endpoints

Sally — thanks for the report and patience. Short version: we see transient egress saturation affecting eu-west-1 BGP peers. We're recommending an immediate application-level region preference change to route production traffic to us-east-1. Steps below are targeted to minimize disruption; we can also execute an automatic reroute for you if you'd like us to do it from our side.

Customer guidance (recommended immediate actions):
1) Quick opt-in (recommended): Set header X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1 on requests. Example: curl -H "X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://model.redwood.example/v1/generate
2) DNS/Client change: If you control DNS, lower TTL and point the region preference to us-east-1.
3) Fallback: Keep apac (ap-southeast-1) as secondary for selected geos if you have significant APAC traffic.

What to expect:
- KV cache: Token-level KV caches are tenant-scoped per model runtime. If you call the us-east-1 model family (same model version), most hot prefixes will still be cacheable but initial misses may increase during and shortly after the switch.
- Session affinity: short-lived sessions will see a small increase in latency during warm-up but no state loss.
- We estimate visible improvement within 5-15 minutes of your switch for most requests; full normalization if provider fixes egress will be 1–3 hours.

We can perform the reroute from our control plane if you prefer — reply with 'please reroute' and a preferred rollback window.

I will follow up shortly with a short post-incident summary and the internal findings.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Sally Torres <sally.torres@pulseai.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.example
Cc: infra@pulseai.com
Date: 2026-08-30T03:34:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx rate and latency spikes affecting EU endpoints

Thanks, Irene.

Please go ahead and execute the reroute from your control plane — we want the minimal ops footprint on our side. Please also confirm whether any in-flight requests will be retried automatically and what we should expect for request ids during the swap.

Appreciate the help — Sally

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.example>
To: Sally Torres <sally.torres@pulseai.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.example, ben.carter@redwood.example, naomi.feldman@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-30T03:48:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx rate and latency spikes affecting EU endpoints

Thanks, Sally — we'll run the control-plane reroute now and monitor. A few notes:
- In-flight requests: we will not drop them deliberately; the control plane issues a graceful drain on affected egress nodes and retries at the proxy layer where feasible. There may be duplicated attempts for some requests; please treat retries as idempotent where possible.
- Request IDs: you may see new request IDs following a retry/resubmit; we will include a correlation mapping in the logs we attach to the postmortem.

I'll confirm when traffic has moved.

—Jordan

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.example>
To: Sally Torres <sally.torres@pulseai.com>
Cc: infra@pulseai.com, ben.carter@redwood.example, jordan.blake@redwood.example, naomi.feldman@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-30T08:47:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary: egress saturation in EU and actions taken

Sally — follow-up and summary after monitoring the environment for the past 5 hours.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:40 — Pulse AI reports elevated 5xx and latency (initial detection).
- 03:05 — Redwood telemetry indicates egress queueing on multiple EU peer interfaces.
- 03:18 — Internal triage; runbook prepared.
- 03:28 — Customer guidance sent; offer to reroute.
- 03:35 — Customer requested control-plane reroute.
- 03:50 — Control-plane reroute initiated; traffic gradually moved to us-east-1.
- 04:10 — Error rates dropped to baseline for most traffic; minor persisted tails until provider reached partial mitigation.

Root cause (preliminary):
- Upstream peering saturation at eu-west-1 (provider-side), likely a transient BGP path flap + over-queued egress due to elevated retransmit behavior.

Mitigation performed:
- Immediate customer opt-in reroute to us-east-1 via control plane.
- Graceful drain of affected egress nodes and proxy-level retry mapping to preserve in-flight requests.
- Additional monitoring rules added to auto-detect similar egress queueing signals and flag affected tenants.

Impact:
- Pulse AI: brief spike in 5xx and tail latency for ~30–45 minutes; most traffic normalized after reroute.
- No data loss detected; cache warm-up increased token usage for ~20 minutes post-swap.

Next steps and longer-term remediation:
1) Engineering (assigned): implement health-based region affinity priming to reduce cold-cache penalty on forced reroutes (owner: Naomi Feldman).
2) Networking (assigned): add more conservative backoff detection for BGP retransmit patterns and automatic early-eviction of affected egress peers (owner: Ben Carter).
3) Customer opt-in flows: create a UI toggle and API call for customers to request provider-side reroutes with a rollback window (owner: Jordan Blake).

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (internal draft), egress-metrics-logs.zip (request-level samples and correlation mapping).

If you'd like a short sync to walk through logs or discuss the rollout window for the UI toggle, I'm available this afternoon. Thanks again for the quick coordination.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
